title: Salt and Crown
premise: Petra Blackwood, a royal food-taster whose body has become a ledger of poisons, hides a forbidden gift: her charms work because she can taste magic like salt on the tongue. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, she learns the court beneath the mountain bought the soul of Tam, the found-family brother who once saved her life, and that the falling wards were the price of that bargain. To reclaim him she must infiltrate the Undercourt as a taster of its king's table, where every dish is a contract and every flavor a debt. Petra ends the story by offering her own seasoned, poison-hardened soul in Tam's place — and discovering that three years of swallowing death have made her indigestible to the dark, breaking the Undercourt's power and returning the stars.
about_author: Ada Kavanagh is a former line cook from a coastal town who claims she learned everything about fantasy by reading menus in six languages. She writes at night, after service, in a kitchen that smells of bay leaves and burnt sugar.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Petra. A routine morning tasting for Queen Maren establishes Petra's world: the poison ledger in her blood, her secret charm-stall in the Nightmarket, and her found family of market orphans. When she tastes arsenic meant for the queen, she also tastes something stranger beneath it — cold, mineral, wrong. Beat: competence and warmth shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Small Charms, Hard Law
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra sells a luck-knot to a dockworker while Wardens patrol for unlicensed magic; her friend Sefa nearly gets caught. That night Tam, her oldest friend, confesses he's been meeting someone from below the mountain. He won't say who. Beat: tenderness fraying under secrets; the law tightening like a fist.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: POV Petra. At midnight the border wards fall with a sound like a struck bell, and every star above the city goes dark at once. The palace erupts; the queen summons Petra through smoke-filled corridors. In the chaos, Tam is gone — his room empty except for a charm Petra made him, split cleanly in two. Beat: terror and vertigo as the known world breaks.

chapters.title: What the Queen Knows
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Queen Maren reveals the truth: three years ago the crown traded a soul to the Undercourt to keep the wards standing, and the payment has come due. The soul was Tam's, sold without his knowledge — or so Maren claims. She orders Petra to find how the trade was brokered. Beat: betrayal of trust in institutions; duty clamping down on grief.

chapters.title: Ledger of Poisons
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Investigating the palace kitchens, Petra discovers the head steward Corvane signed the original pact — and that his ledgers list her own name as 'reserve collateral.' She realizes the queen may have always intended her as backup payment. Beat: paranoia; the sick taste of being currency rather than person.

chapters.title: The Market Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Through Sefa's eyes we see Petra from outside: reckless, grieving, burning her charms for cash to bribe a Warden archivist. The market family argues whether to help her flee the city or follow her down. Beat: found family tested by fear; love expressed as argument.

chapters.title: Down the Stair of Teeth
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Following Corvane's records, Petra finds the old toll-gate into the mountain and descends past wards made of fused bone. Each threshold demands a memory as toll; she pays with the taste of her mother's bread. Beat: sacrifice begins; wonder curdled into horror.

chapters.title: A Table Set for One More
chapters.summary: POV Petra. In the Undercourt, souls serve as servants, and Petra bluffs her way into the king's kitchen by identifying — by taste alone — seven poisons in a single broth. The Underking's steward, a hollow-eyed woman named Vess, takes notice. Beat: audacity; Petra weaponizing the very skill her suffering built.

chapters.title: Flavors of the Dead
chapters.summary: POV Vess. Vess, once a taster herself, recognizes what Petra is and what it cost. She warns Petra that the Underking eats contracts, not food, and that Tam's soul is already half-dissolved into the mountain's foundations. Beat: uneasy mentorship; two women mirrored across decades of servitude.

chapters.title: The King Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Summoned to taste for the Underking, Petra meets him: courteous, ancient, starving. He offers her a place at his table forever in exchange for Tam's debt being 'transferred.' She tastes his offer and finds it laced with something that feels like home — the most dangerous poison yet. Beat: temptation dressed as belonging.

chapters.title: Half a Soul Still Sings
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Guided by Vess, Petra reaches the vault where Tam's soul is kept in a jar of starlight — the last light in a starless world. His fragment recognizes her and hums the market's street-song. Beat: heartbreak and hope entwined; proof that love persists in fragments.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Corvane. The steward, dying of a pact-backlash, admits he sold Tam's name to save his daughter — and that the queen knew and allowed it. He gives Petra the one flaw in the Underking's contracts: no soul freely offered can be taken twice. Beat: moral ruin revealed; even villains are people who chose badly.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage Back
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Above ground, Sefa and the market family breach the sealed toll-gate with smuggled charms, refusing to let Petra face the mountain alone. Their descent costs them: the youngest, Pip, loses her voice to a ward-toll. Beat: found family choosing danger over safety; loyalty made literal.

chapters.title: A Feast of Debts
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The Underking hosts a banquet where each course rebinds an old contract. Petra serves the final dish herself, laced with a charm keyed to Tam's song. The mountain shudders; the king tastes the trick and smiles — he expected nothing less. Beat: gambit exposed; dread before the fall.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Hunger
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Captured, Petra negotiates: her soul, seasoned by three years of poisons, for Tam's. The Underking accepts because her essence promises a flavor he's never tasted. Vess secretly slips Petra a knife of ward-iron. Beat: the terrible calm of self-sacrifice; love against duty made explicit.

chapters.title: The Tasting
chapters.summary: POV Petra. At the moment of exchange, the Underking drinks Petra's offered soul and recoils — she is saturated with death, bitter as ash, indigestible. Her poison-tempered nature begins to unravel his hunger from the inside. Beat: climax turns on identity; the thing that made her expendable makes her unconquerable.

chapters.title: Starlight Unbound
chapters.summary: POV Petra and Tam. With the king convulsing, Petra shatters the jar; Tam's soul floods back into his body as Sefa's family fights through to the hall. Vess chooses this moment to open the Undercourt's gates, letting centuries of stolen souls pour toward the surface. Beat: catharsis; the rescue becoming a liberation.

chapters.title: The Mountain Exhales
chapters.summary: POV Vess. Vess holds the collapsing Underking's attention while the others climb, paying her own long-held soul back into the mountain willingly — the first free gift it has ever received. The Undercourt's foundation cracks. Beat: redemption through sacrifice; quiet heroism at the center of the storm.

chapters.title: Ascension
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The survivors climb the Stair of Teeth as it crumbles, Petra carrying the weakening Tam, paying memories she can't spare. They break the surface just as dawn arrives — and with it, the stars fading back into a brightening sky, visible one last time like embers. Beat: exhaustion, relief, grief for those left behind.

chapters.title: Reckoning at Court
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra stands before Queen Maren with Corvane's confession and the surviving market family as witnesses. She refuses a title, demands the outlawing of small magics be repealed, and walks out of the throne room to applause she didn't ask for. Beat: power declined; justice claimed without corruption taking root.

chapters.title: Salt in the Bread
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Recovering slowly, Tam bakes in the market kitchen, relearning his own appetites. He and Petra circle each other awkwardly — both changed, both guilty of surviving. Over shared bread he asks why she came for him; she says the truth: there was never a version of the world where she didn't. Beat: tender resolution; love spoken plainly at last.

chapters.title: The First Star
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Months later, the Nightmarket sells charms openly, and Petra teaches young tasters to read flavors safely. On the anniversary of the dark night, the first new star kindles above the mountain — Vess's gift, perhaps, or the mountain learning generosity. Petra raises a cup of salted honey wine to the sky. Beat: renewal; wounds honored, future opened.
